provenance: One text encoder or VAE sits inside dozens of unrelated bundles, so a content-hash lookup on a community site returns whichever bundle somebody uploaded first, and that stranger's permission flags then decide the licence of a file they did not publish. Each entry here is a file whose sha256 was traced back to the repository that actually publishes it, together with the licence tag that repository declares. Entries are added one misjudged case at a time; a mirror, a re-upload or a guess is not a source.
components_note: Empty is the correct starting state, not an oversight: this table only ever releases, so an empty table releases nothing and every file keeps the deny-by-default answer. Entries arrive through the signed rules channel, which is the whole point of putting them here rather than in code - a shared part judged wrongly is fixed for everyone without a release. Each entry needs sha256, origin_url and spdx; the reader in licensing.py refuses any entry whose origin is not an authority it recognises or whose licence is not one we already pass on, so adding a row cannot widen either of those.
